precepts.text: Solomon was wiser than Ethan, Heman, Chalcol and Darda, the sons of Zarah; he surpassed even the wise men of his own tribe.
precepts.point: Hezron begat Ram, Ram begat Amminadab, Amminadab begat Nahshon the prince of the children of Judah, and from Nahshon come Salma, Boaz, Obed and Jesse.

note.label: The Nativity: the Bloodline, Birthright, & the Messiah

precepts.why:
Judah had five sons: Er, Onan and Shelah by the daughter of Shua the Canaanitess, and the twins Pharez and Zerah by Tamar. “The sons of Pharez; Hezron, and Hamul. And the sons of Zerah; Zimri, and Ethan, and Heman, and Calcol, and Dara: five of them in all.” Ethan, Heman, Calcol and Dara became very famous. They were very wise.

How wise? Solomon’s wisdom is measured against them: “For he was wiser than all men; than Ethan the Ezrahite, and Heman, and Chalcol, and Darda, the sons of Mahol: and his fame was in all nations round about.”

Those same sons of Judah were so wise that many men were named after them, and Solomon surpassed even them. He was wiser than the wise men of his own tribe.

That is the house this genealogy runs through. Hezron, the oldest son of Pharez, begat Ram, and from Ram comes Amminadab, Nahshon, Salma, Boaz, Obed and Jesse: a tribe of wise men, princes and kings.

precepts.text: Nahshon the son of Amminadab was captain of the children of Judah; these were princes and captains, not ordinary men, and Boaz came from that line.
precepts.point: Hezron begat Ram, Ram begat Amminadab, Amminadab begat Nahshon the prince of the children of Judah, and from Nahshon come Salma, Boaz, Obed and Jesse.

note.label: The Nativity: the Bloodline, Birthright, & the Messiah

precepts.why:
“And Ram begat Amminadab; and Amminadab begat Nahshon, prince of the children of Judah”. Nahshon was of the elite princes of Judah, a prince family, a royal family. The census confirms the same man: “Of Judah; Nahshon the son of Amminadab.”

And in the camp: “And on the east side toward the rising of the sun shall they of the standard of the camp of Judah pitch throughout their armies: and Nahshon the son of Amminadab shall be captain of the children of Judah.”

So Nahshon was a captain. These men had serious status: princes and captains, leaders. They were warriors; they were not regular men.

“And Nahshon begat Salma, and Salma begat Boaz, And Boaz begat Obed, and Obed begat Jesse”. Boaz came from that line, the line of Pharez, the twin that breached, not the one whose hand came out first with the scarlet thread. And Jesse had eight sons, and one of those sons is David.

precepts.text: Aaron took Elisheba, Amminadab's daughter and Nahshon's sister, to wife; priests and kings intermarried, which is why John the Baptist and Christ are cousins, and why Eleazar the high priest had a mother of Judah.
precepts.point: Hezron begat Ram, Ram begat Amminadab, Amminadab begat Nahshon the prince of the children of Judah, and from Nahshon come Salma, Boaz, Obed and Jesse.

note.label: The Nativity: the Bloodline, Birthright, & the Messiah

precepts.why:
Now a tie-in regarding family ties: “And Aaron took him Elisheba, daughter of Amminadab, sister of Naashon, to wife; and she bare him Nadab, and Abihu, Eleazar, and Ithamar.”

Aaron is Moses’ brother, of Levi. He took Elisheba, Amminadab’s daughter and Nahshon’s sister, to wife. Aaron’s wife was of the tribe of Judah. Those families intermarried, priests and kings marrying together. It is no coincidence; that is why John the Baptist and Christ are cousins.

Nadab and Abihu were the two who offered strange fire and were killed; Eleazar and Ithamar were spared. Eleazar became the high priest in the days of Joshua, the mediator before the Lord. So Eleazar’s mama was Judah. That is why some Levites don’t have the big heads; their mama is Judah. And don’t forget the big nose, too.

So Amminadab begat Nahshon and a daughter Elisheba. Aaron married Elisheba and had the four sons, the high priests, which makes Nahshon Aaron’s brother-in-law. And from Nahshon came Salma, Boaz, Obed and Jesse: the priesthood and the royal line of Judah bound together in one family.

precepts.text: Abram, childless, meant to leave his house to Eliezer of Damascus, the eldest servant born in his house; the Lord said this shall not be thine heir, but he that shall come forth out of thine own bowels; an heir and an inheritance are the same word.
precepts.point: It is written there to exclude, not to include; it does not mean the Egyptian became a Jew, and when we came back under the Persians a man who could not show his father's house got no inheritance and no office.

note.label: The Nativity: the Bloodline, Birthright, & the Messiah

precepts.why:
Abram, childless, was going to leave his house to Eliezer of Damascus, the eldest servant born in his house: “Behold, to me thou hast given no seed: and, lo, one born in my house is mine heir.” The Lord said no: “This shall not be thine heir; but he that shall come forth out of thine own bowels shall be thine heir.” Not a heathen servant, but his own seed. An heir and an inheritance are the same word, like a family heirloom passed down the line.

That is the key to 1 Chronicles 2: “Now Sheshan had no sons, but daughters. And Sheshan had a servant, an Egyptian, whose name was Jarha. And Sheshan gave his daughter to Jarha his servant to wife.” This was while Israel was in Egypt, when we had no land of inheritance allotted to us. People read it and say the Egyptian married into the tribe and became Judah. No.

The record follows that line for generation after generation so that it is known. When Israel came out of Egypt and inherited the land, that line could not receive land, because the land passes by the paternal bloodline and that line goes back to an Egyptian servant. They were among us in the land, but they did not inherit. It is written there to exclude, not to include. Sheshan's brothers had sons and received land; his line did not. It does not mean the Egyptian became a Jew. When we came back under the Persians and the Medes, a man who could not show from his father's house who he came from was given no inheritance, and a Levite could not serve in his office. Zerubbabel could show he came from King David's line.

The daughters of Zelophehad show the law when a man has only daughters. They asked, “Why should the name of our father be done away from among his family, because he hath no son?” The Lord said, “If a man die, and have no son, then ye shall cause his inheritance to pass unto his daughter”, then to his brother, then his father's brethren, then the next kinsman: the law Boaz was fulfilling. But those daughters had to marry “only to the family of the tribe of their father”, “So shall not the inheritance of the children of Israel remove from tribe to tribe.” The inheritance of Israel is paternal. There is no sin in marrying a woman of another tribe; Aaron did it. The command there was only to keep the land in the tribe. We have no land in captivity now, so marry within your nation and stay with your people.

precepts.text: The children of Israel that came into Egypt with Jacob are named, the same sons listed here.
precepts.point: The nations call us a minority and divide us by many labels so they can deal wisely with us, but we are not a minority, and the Most High promised to multiply our seed like the stars of heaven and the sand of the sea.

note.label: 1 Chronicles 2: The Sons of Israel and the Line of Judah

precepts.why:
“Now these are the names of the children of Israel, which came into Egypt; every man and his household came with Jacob.” These are the same sons listed in Chronicles: “Reuben, Simeon, Levi, and Judah, Issachar, and Zebulun, Dan, Joseph, and Benjamin, Naphtali, Gad, and Asher.”

These are the sons of Jacob that came into Egypt, and we carry their name, their lineage, and their descent from the twelve tribes of Israel.

precepts.text: It is a great love and an honor that we should be called the sons of God, though the world knows us not.
precepts.point: The nations call us a minority and divide us by many labels so they can deal wisely with us, but we are not a minority, and the Most High promised to multiply our seed like the stars of heaven and the sand of the sea.

note.label: 1 Chronicles 2: The Sons of Israel and the Line of Judah

precepts.why:
“Behold, what manner of love the Father hath bestowed upon us, that we should be called the sons of God: therefore the world knoweth us not, because it knew him not.” It is a great love and an honor that we should be called the sons of God.

The world knows us not. The nations call us a minority and divide us by many labels so they can deal wisely with us. But we are not a minority. We are “the sons of Israel”, and the Most High promised to multiply our seed like the stars of heaven and the sand of the sea.

precepts.text: Inquire of the former age and prepare thyself to the search of thy fathers, for it matters whose son you are.
precepts.point: The nations call us a minority and divide us by many labels so they can deal wisely with us, but we are not a minority, and the Most High promised to multiply our seed like the stars of heaven and the sand of the sea.

note.label: 1 Chronicles 2: The Sons of Israel and the Line of Judah

precepts.why:
“For enquire, I pray thee, of the former age, and prepare thyself to the search of their fathers”. It matters whose son you are.

That is why the record sets down “the sons of Israel” by name. When we search out our fathers, we find these twelve, and we carry their name, their lineage and their descent.

precepts.text: Judah took the daughter of Shua the Canaanite, who bare him Er, Onan, and Shelah.
precepts.point: This is why the counsel is to desire not a multitude of unprofitable children, for an evil son is not counted in the record.

note.label: 1 Chronicles 2: The Sons of Israel and the Line of Judah

precepts.why:
“And Judah saw there a daughter of a certain Canaanite, whose name was Shuah; and he took her, and went in unto her.” She bare him Er, Onan and Shelah, the three “born unto him of the daughter of Shua the Canaanitess.” Pharez and Zerah he had of Tamar his daughter in law.

“Er, the firstborn of Judah, was evil in the sight of the Lord; and he slew him.” Just as Cain was evil and is passed over in the genealogy of the sons of God, an evil son is not counted in the record. This is why the counsel is to desire not a multitude of unprofitable children.

precepts.text: The Most High names Jezreel to declare He will avenge the blood of Jezreel upon the house of Jehu.
precepts.point: Names in this line carry meaning, as when the Most High named the children of Hosea to declare His judgment on the house of Israel.

note.label: 1 Chronicles 2: The Sons of Israel and the Line of Judah

precepts.why:
“And the Lord said unto him, Call his name Jezreel; for yet a little while, and I will avenge the blood of Jezreel upon the house of Jehu, and will cause to cease the kingdom of the house of Israel.” The Most High named the child Jezreel to declare His judgment.

Names in the line of Jerahmeel carry meaning the same way. The record names his sons through his wives, Ram, Onam, Shammai, Jada and the rest, and keeps account even of the branches that did not continue: “Seled died without children”, and “Jether died without children.”

precepts.text: The Most High names Lo-ruhamah, for He will no more have mercy upon the house of Israel.
precepts.point: Names in this line carry meaning, as when the Most High named the children of Hosea to declare His judgment on the house of Israel.

note.label: 1 Chronicles 2: The Sons of Israel and the Line of Judah

precepts.why:
“And she conceived again, and bare a daughter. And God said unto him, Call her name Lo–ruhamah: for I will no more have mercy upon the house of Israel; but I will utterly take them away.” The Most High named her Lo-ruhamah, for He would no more have mercy upon the house of Israel.

The name itself declares the judgment. That is how names carry meaning in scripture, and why the names in this line of Judah are set down one by one.

precepts.text: The congregation declared their pedigrees after their families, by the house of their fathers.
precepts.point: Pedigrees are declared by the house of the fathers, so the line is reckoned through the father even here.

note.label: 1 Chronicles 2: The Sons of Israel and the Line of Judah

precepts.why:
“And they assembled all the congregation together on the first day of the second month, and they declared their pedigrees after their families, by the house of their fathers”. Pedigrees are declared by the house of the fathers.

“Now Sheshan had no sons, but daughters.” He gave his daughter “to Jarha his servant to wife”, an Egyptian, “and she bare him Attai.” The line is carried down from their child, and even here it is reckoned through the father: Attai begat Nathan, Nathan begat Zabad, and on down to Elishama.

points: The sons of Judah are named: Er, Onan, and Shelah, born to him of the daughter of Shua the Canaanitess, and then Perez and Zerah, born to him of Tamar his daughter-in-law.
Er, the firstborn of Judah, was evil in the sight of the Most High, and he slew him, just as Cain was evil and is passed over in the genealogy of the sons of God.

note.label: 1 Chronicles 2: The Sons of Israel and the Line of Judah

points: The line runs from Perez through his sons Hezron and Hamul, and the sons of Zerah are named, five in all.

note.label: 1 Chronicles 2: The Sons of Israel and the Line of Judah

points: Achar, called the troubler of Israel, is set in the record as the one who transgressed in the accursed thing, a warning kept alongside the names.

note.label: 1 Chronicles 2: The Sons of Israel and the Line of Judah

note.label: 1 Chronicles 2: The Sons of Israel and the Line of Judah

points: Jesse's sons are set down in order, with David named the seventh, and his sisters Zeruiah and Abigail.
The sons of Zeruiah, Abishai, Joab, and Asahel, are named, and Amasa the son of Abigail, whose father was Jether the Ishmaelite.

note.label: 1 Chronicles 2: The Sons of Israel and the Line of Judah

note.label: 1 Chronicles 2: The Sons of Israel and the Line of Judah

points: Every one of these names carries significance; two picked at random were found to mean father of salvation and hearing and obeying, and much of this line appears in the lineage of Christ.
